text:
[title] Why serving is hard
[body] Every request grows a KV-cache as it generates tokens
[body] Fragmented memory wastes GPU capacity
[body] Tail latency (p99) is what users feel

novice.takeaway: The slide lists three technical reasons why serving AI models efficiently is difficult: growing memory needs, wasted capacity, and slow worst-case response times.
questions: How does p99 relate to average latency?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to understand the key technical challenges their system solves.

peer.takeaway: Serving LLM requests is difficult because growing memory caches, memory fragmentation, and tail latency all strain GPU resources and user experience.
questions: What exactly is a KV-cache technically?
How does fragmentation specifically waste GPU capacity?
How do these three issues connect to the 2.4x claim?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants to justify why their solution's improvements in serving efficiency matter.

expert.takeaway: The slide outlines three core challenges in LLM serving—growing KV-cache, memory fragmentation, and tail latency—that motivate the improvement claimed on the title slide.
questions: Will PagedAttention or similar be presented as the fix?
How does fragmentation quantitatively affect throughput here?
What baseline system exhibits these problems?
expert.inferred_claim: These three problems are the key obstacles the presenter's system solves to achieve the 2.4x p99 goodput gain.
